ai.title: Fix experimental mode to use Sonnet
ai.summary: The `getModelForMode` function in `common/src/constants.ts` was updated to correctly route the `experimental` cost mode to `claudeModels.sonnet` instead of `gemini2_5_pro_exp`. This reverts an unintended regression where the experimental flag failed to select the expected agent model. The change affects core model resolution logic for all surfaces using the shared constants. Whitespace in `UserState` comments was also normalized.

eli5.text: When you run the software with the experimental setting turned on, the assistant will now use a different helper model than it did before. The experimental option had been accidentally sending requests to the wrong helper and falling back to an unexpected one instead; that is now fixed so the experimental flag picks the right helper again. Only people using the experimental mode are affected, and nothing about regular or budget modes changed.

ai.title: Record model in main prompt logs
ai.summary: Adds `model` to the metadata objects passed to the logging calls in `mainPrompt` within `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This change ensures the active model is recorded in both the initial prompt log (`Main prompt`) and the response log (`Main prompt response`). The update is internal, affecting only logging instrumentation without altering user-facing behavior or API responses.

eli5.text: The system now quietly writes down which version of the assistant was active in its internal notes whenever it starts and finishes a conversation turn. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment to the logging tool that does not change how the assistant behaves or what it tells you, and you will not see any difference unless you are digging through the raw log files.

ai.title: BigQuery trace logging for file selection
ai.summary: Adds `common/src/bigquery/client.ts` and `schema.ts` to log agent steps, file requests, and search prompts to BigQuery. Backend initializes the client on startup and inserts traces with `agent_step_id` correlation in `main-prompt.ts` and `search-system-prompt.ts`. Includes `scripts/ft-file-selection` tooling for data collection and relabeling. Tables use monthly partitioning and clustering on `user_id` and `agent_step_id`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to help find or use files in your project, the system now records a detailed log of every step it takes, which files it looked at, what it searched for, and in what order † to a secure database. This gives the team invisible breadcrumbs to trace exactly why the assistant picked certain files or skipped others, even mid-task. The change is live today for everyone running the assistant through the web interface; if you use it, each of your sessions is now quietly being logged behind the scenes so problems (like a missing file or a slow search) can be investigated later. There are no visible differences in how the assistant behaves right now, it just gains the ability to be understood better if something goes wrong.

ai.title: CI wraps test steps with retry@v3
ai.summary: CI wraps npm-app, backend, and common test steps with nick-fields/retry@v3. Retry handles flaky tests. Each step gets 10-minute timeout, 5 max attempts.

eli5.text: The project now automatically retries individual test suites when they fail unexpectedly, rather than failing the entire build on the first problem. Each retry attempt runs for up to ten minutes, and the system will try up to five times before declaring a failure. This helps prevent unrelated hiccups, like temporary network blips, from breaking progress checks and keeps the automated validation process more reliable. Only those who trigger the validation workflow would notice the difference, primarily that genuine failures are easier to distinguish from transient ones.

ai.title: Disable stored API key fetching in client
ai.summary: Client initialization no longer fetches stored API key types from /api/api-keys; logic commented out, `storedApiKeyTypes` defaults to empty array. Removes unused `GrantType` import and `gray` color dependency. Formatting adjustment to auto top-up log output. Internal change in `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: When the app starts up, it no longer tries to look up your saved API key types from a remote server; instead, it just assumes you don't have any stored keys yet. If you were watching the startup process or checking the console, you'd see that step is gone and the feature simply starts with an empty list. This is currently live for anyone using the latest version of the app. Behind the scenes, this also cleaned out some unused code and simplified a log message that shows when your account gets automatically topped up with credits.

ai.title: Pricing page credit visual and layout
ai.summary: Pricing page `CreditVisual` component updated to add 500-credit usage context and adjust spacing. Tooltip imports added to `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx`. PricingCard container refactored for full-height flex layout.

eli5.text: The pricing page now explains what 500 credits actually buy you: roughly a full day of heavy coding on a new project, shown in a small note right under the price. The price display itself is tighter and more centered, and the pricing cards now stretch to the same height so columns line up evenly. If you visit the pricing page today, you'll see a clearer, more balanced layout with that usage hint added.

ai.summary: The `--model` CLI option help text in `npm-app/src/index.ts` now lists `o4-mini` and `o3` as valid arguments, replacing `o3-mini`. This internal update aligns the experimental model picker with current available models. A debug `console.log` statement was also added to the CLI startup sequence.

eli5.text: When you run the tool from the command line and ask it to list or pick a model, you will now see two newer model names appear where an older one used to be, so you can point the assistant at the updated options. This only affects people who explicitly choose a model for experimental runs; if you never touch that option, you will not notice any difference. The change is already live today.

ai.title: Add enabled flag to startupProcesses config schema
ai.summary: Introduced `enabled` boolean (default true) to `StartupProcessSchema` in `constants.ts`. `dev-process-manager.ts` now skips execution for disabled processes via early continue. This allows conditional process startup without removing entries from config.

eli5.text: The list of programs that starts up in your development environment can now include an on/off switch next to each one. When a program is marked off, the startup process quietly skips over it instead of launching, so you can keep an entry in the list for later without having to take it out. This affects anyone configuring these startup programs in their settings. You'd notice the change only when you look at the settings: a previously required yes/no value that used to be assumed is now explicitly written in.

ai.title: Remove subscription column from user export script
ai.summary: The `scripts/export-user-emails.ts` script no longer queries or includes `subscription_active` in the CSV output. This reduces the export to `Email`, `Name`, and `Created At`. The change simplifies the data selection logic and removes the boolean-to-string conversion for the subscription status.

eli5.text: When someone exports the list of user emails, the spreadsheet no longer includes a column showing whether each user has an active subscription. If you open the exported file, you will see only the email address, the user's name, and the date they signed up, instead of the previous four columns that also had a 'Yes' or 'No' for subscription status. This is now in effect, so anyone running the export will get the simpler version.

ai.title: Admin file-picker relabel page and BigQuery column fixes
ai.summary: New internal admin page at /admin/.../file-picker allows manual triggering of trace relabeling for specific users. Backend adds relabelForUser endpoint with CORS support to process get-relevant-files traces via Claude and Gemini. BigQuery client queries updated to use snake_case column names (created_at, agent_step_id, user_id) matching actual schema, fixing potential query failures. Relabel script now processes traces in parallel batches of 5.

eli5.text: You now have a new admin page where staff can manually ask the system to re-label or analyze file-picker activity for a specific user. When triggered, the system pulls relevant traces for that user and runs them through two AI models (Claude and Gemini) in small parallel batches, then stores the new labels in BigQuery. The database column names used in queries were also corrected to match the actual schema (created_at, agent_step_id, user_id), fixing potential query errors. This is live today in the admin interface.

ai.title: Inject Codebuff config schema into agent system prompt
ai.summary: Moved `json-config` modules from `npm-app` to `common` package to allow backend access. `getAgentSystemPrompt` now injects `CodebuffConfigSchema` stringified via `stringifySchemaForLLM` into the prompt, enabling the agent to interpret user settings from `.codebuffrc.json`. Token counts for the new schema prompt are tracked in `configSchemaTokens` and included in the final system prompt build.

eli5.text: When you ask Codebuff to work on your project, it now receives a clear, built-in description of which settings it is allowed to read from your.codebuffrc.json file, so it no longer has to guess or misread the configuration options you typed. Codebuff can now understand your personalized settings, like style preferences or model choices, directly from that file and apply them correctly while helping you. This works live today, so the next time you run Codebuff, it should respond more accurately to the config file you've already set up.

ai.title: Add JSON schema descriptions for config file
ai.summary: Added `.describe()` calls to `StartupProcessSchema` and `CodebuffConfigSchema` in `constants.ts` to provide human-readable documentation for config fields. Implemented `stringify-schema.ts` to recursively convert Zod schemas into a formatted text representation, handling optional, default, object, and array types. This internal change improves developer understanding of the `codebuff.json` structure without altering runtime validation logic.

eli5.text: Nothing you can see or touch has changed in the app today; this work is purely for developers maintaining the code. The team added plain-language explanations to the configuration files so that when someone looks at or generates documentation for the config structure, they see helpful descriptions of each setting instead of bare field names and types. These descriptions are now stored alongside the field definitions and a new utility can turn the whole schema into readable text, but that text never appears in the running application or affects how configuration is validated.

ai.title: Startup process stdoutFile stderrFile redirect
ai.summary: Added `stdoutFile` and `stderrFile` to `StartupProcessSchema` in `common/src/json-config/constants.ts`. `runBackgroundCommand` in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` creates write streams for these paths, resolving relative paths against `projectPath` and creating directories. `dev-process-manager.ts` passes these options to the background runner. `.gitignore` updated to ignore all `**.log` files.

eli5.text: When this software starts up certain background tools it runs, each tool's text output (like status messages or errors) now gets saved to its own log file instead of just being shown on screen. For example the tool that shows the database browser writes its output to a file called drizzle.log so it's easier to find later. The system also now ignores all files ending in.log so these don't clutter or interfere with other parts of the project.
